New race calls are strengthening Democratic gains.
In North Carolina, the AP announced several congressional races for Democrats in districts
that were once considered safely Republican, the North Carolina newsroom's Adam Wagner
reports from Raleigh.
The AP has called North Carolina's 6th, 9th, 13th, and 14th districts for Democrats Cyril
Jefferson, Richard Ojeda, Paul Behringer, and Lakeisha Womack.
They're all seats where Republicans won by significant margins in 2024, a sign of this
year's blue wave.
Democrats have now flipped five of North Carolina's 14 U.S. House seats.
And in eastern North Carolina, Republicans redrew the first congressional district as
part of this year's mid-decade redistricting in an effort to defeat incumbent Democrat
Don Davis.
Yet Davis defeated repeat challenger Lori Buck out, actually winning by a larger margin
than he did in 2024.
There are five remaining North Carolina districts to be called, with Democrats leading in one.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Wagner, in Raleigh.
First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House today,
and Paris Franco-Ordonez reports they recognized a temporary ceasefire she helped broker in
Ukraine.
The administration is touting the recent pause around the city of Olesky as a diplomatic
breakthrough as they ramp up efforts to secure an agreement to end the war in Ukraine.
Melania Trump said she hopes the agreement can serve as a spark that leads to something
more enduring.
We have chosen humanity over war.
Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war.
The six-day pause in fighting allowed humanitarian aid to reach residents, as well as allow hundreds

Franco-Ordonez, NPR News, the White House.
Mass protests have drawn huge crowds across France, demanding higher wages and supporting
the student protest movement.
France's Interior Ministry says more than 600,000 people rallied today.
A major union said nearly 1.6 million people participated nationwide.
About a third of France's high schools were closed and public transportation was disrupted.
Authorities deployed 70,000 police officers amid tensions.
The movement began in September and has spread nationwide.
This is NPR News.
Harmeet Dylan, a conservative attorney who oversaw a radical reshaping of the Justice
Department's Civil Rights Division, has resigned.
Dylan has been a powerful and divisive figure inside President Trump's Justice Department
since her confirmation last year as Assistant Attorney General.
She dramatically changed the direction of the division, created to protect the rights
of minorities.
Watching aggression can rewire the brain to be ready to fight.
That's the finding in a new study on mice.
As NPR's Pink Wong reports, it involved staged cage matches.
Mice that watched a series of staged cage fights, but had never fought themselves, showed
changes in their brains similar to those with actual fighting experience.
Anna-Gret Faulkner is with the Princeton Neuroscience Institute.
Watching doesn't get you the whole way there, but it does quite a fair bit and it does it
all in the right direction.
Later, when the spectator mice had their own fights, they were more vigilant and used aggression
and defense strategies they picked up from watching both sides of the battle.
Their brain activity showed they had less inhibition, fewer neurons saying stop.
Faulkner says this demonstrates how just watching something can lead to changes in brain wiring
and behavior.
The paper is published in the journal Nature, Ping Huang, NPR News.
This year's Rockefeller Center Christmas tree has been cut down in West Edmiston, New

The 76-foot Norway Spruce is expected to arrive Saturday.
The tree will be wrapped with over 50,000 lights and crowned with a 900-pound star before
lighting up during a live broadcast ceremony on December 2nd.
The tree will be on display until January 9th, after which it will be milled into lumber
for Habitat for Humanity.
